interpretations: 这份虚构答卷全部选择中立／不确定。相反的回答也可能在同一条轴上互相抵消，出现相同的中点。

faq: 8 Values 是哪个版本？
本站改编自 8values 开源项目固定修订的 70 道题，保留英文题干和原始有符号权重。中文由费马翻译。
为什么四条轴有八个结果名称？
经济轴是平等／市场，外交轴是全球／国家，公民轴是公民自由／权威，社会轴是进步／传统。每条轴的两个显示端相加等于 100%。
一题能同时影响几条轴吗？
可以。选项乘数为 −1、−0.5、0、+0.5、+1，同一个乘数会应用到这条陈述的每个轴权重。负权重使贡献方向反转。
50% 表示中间派吗？
中立或不确定的作答可以得到 50%，方向相反的贡献相抵也可以。小数差来自固定题本换算及四舍五入，无法据此判断立场、人口百分位或投票选择。
测试免费吗？题目可以跳过吗？
全部结果和八篇公开指南均免费且免注册。须答完 70 道题才产生本次数轴结果。可以随时退出后直接阅读指南。
分享链接会显示我的答案或得分吗？
复制的是公开入口链接，不包含答案、百分数或个人标识。现有分享不生成个人 PNG。
zh.formula: 每题选项乘数是 −1、−0.5、0、+0.5、+1。把乘数与各轴有符号权重相乘后按轴求和 S。四轴绝对权重总和 M 依次为 195、225、320、292。正向计分端为 100 × (M + S) ÷ (2 × M)，保留一位小数，另一端为 100 减去已显示的值。
zh.boundary: 保留固定来源的 70 道英文原题、五个选项和计分权重，中文为费马译文。这些结果只描述受答题情境影响的个人回答，尚无独立的翻译等值、信度或人口常模数据，也不输出政党、投票建议或固定的意识形态。

faq: 這個 8 Values 測驗來自哪裡？
題目沿用 8values 開源專案固定版本的 70 題，保留原英文和正負權重。中文由費馬翻譯。
為什麼四條量尺會有八個名稱？
經濟軸是平等／市場、外交軸是全球／國家、公民軸是公民自由／權威、社會軸是進步／傳統。每一軸都會顯示兩端，加起來是 100%。
勾一個選項可能影響多條量尺嗎？
可能。作答乘數依序為 −1、−0.5、0、+0.5、+1，每個乘數會套用在該陳述的各軸權重上。負權重的貢獻方向會相反。
50% 就是立場居中嗎？
選中立／不確定，或兩種方向的答案相抵，都能得到 50%。這個數字無法用來判定政治身分、人口百分等級或投票選擇。
需要付費嗎？可以跳著做嗎？
免註冊，結果和八篇公開指南都免費。完整回答 70 道題才會產生個人分數，也可以直接閱讀公開指南。
轉傳連結時會公開作答內容嗎？
複製的是公開測驗入口，連結不會附上答案、百分比或作答者資料。現在沒有個人 PNG 分享圖卡。
zh-TW.formula: 每題以 −1、−0.5、0、+0.5、+1 與各軸正負權重相乘，同軸加總得到 S。四軸的權重絕對值總和 M 依序為 195、225、320、292。正向計分端是 100 × (M + S) ÷ (2 × M)，顯示到小數點後一位，另一端用 100 減去顯示值。
zh-TW.boundary: 費馬保留固定版本的 70 道英文原題、選項與計分權重，另行提供中文翻譯。這份測驗還沒有單獨驗證翻譯等值、信度和人口常模。結果只整理這次的作答，不分派政黨、固定意識形態或投票建議。

en.facts: The FermatMind 8 Values Political Test adapts a fixed revision of the original 70-item questionnaire and takes about 15 minutes. No account or payment is required. After all 70 answers, it shows four pairs of complementary percentages and the weighted sums behind them. Eight public guides explain the endpoints and how to read the results. Sharing copies only the public test link.
en.intro: Your views on public services may differ from how you think about international cooperation, individual freedom, or customs. Respond to 70 statements in about 15 minutes and read four two-ended scales, with eight guides you can open any time. The test is free and requires no account.
deliverables: Read the economic, diplomatic, civil, and societal axes separately. Each pair adds to 100%, and you can also view its raw weighted sum.
Read all eight guides for free
The endpoint guides describe the questions and trade-offs relevant to each pair. You can read any guide without completing the test.
The link opens the public test page in your language. It carries no answers, percentages, or details that identify your attempt.
interpretations: Every answer in this sample is neutral or unsure. The same midpoint can also arise when answers contribute in opposite directions and cancel.
One answer changes: two axes move
Choose Strongly Agree for item 6 and Neutral/Unsure for the other 69. Equality displays 51.3%, Liberty 48.4%, and both other axes remain at 50.0 / 50.0.
Scoring boundary: 100.0% on the Progress end

Use the strongest matching choice for every signed societal effect and neutral for zero effects. Equality, Globe, Liberty, and Progress display 64.1%, 67.8%, 71.9%, and 100.0%. This is a synthetic scoring illustration.

equality: You can use the Equality guide to revisit what you considered in questions about public provision, distribution, and intervention.
When a town considers a fare discount, you might compare a universal price cut with targeted help.
markets: What prices and competition can do
You can use the Markets guide to revisit questions about prices, private enterprise, and rules for competition.
As a market reopens, you might compare letting more sellers in with giving all sellers the same operating terms.
nation: When decisions stay within a nation
You can use the Nation guide to revisit questions about domestic obligations, resources, or independent decisions.
When discussing a joint project across borders, you might ask how local commitments can be managed.
globe: What can be done across borders
You can use the Globe guide to revisit the situations in which sharing resources or coordinating decisions felt workable.
When two countries share a river, you might compare separate cleanups with a joint effort to monitor water quality.
liberty: You can use the Liberty guide to revisit questions that led you to consider privacy, choice, and procedural safeguards.
When a public venue proposes keeping visitor records, you might ask which details are needed and when they should be deleted.
authority: You can use the Authority guide to revisit which situations drew your attention to common rules and enforcement.
If noise near an event space disturbs residents, you might compare an informal agreement with a fixed closing rule.
progress: When a familiar practice is worth revisiting
You can use the Progress guide to revisit which questions prompted you to reconsider an established practice.
When a public event adds online registration, you might check whom the change makes it easier or harder to attend.
tradition: What remains useful from an older practice
You can use the Tradition guide to consider when continuity, customs, or experience mattered in your answers.
If a neighborhood event changes its schedule, you might ask what the existing format has helped residents do.

faq: Which version of 8 Values is this?
This adaptation uses the original English statements and signed weights from a fixed 70-item revision of the open-source 8values project. FermatMind supplies the Chinese translations.
Why are there four axes and eight labels?
The pairs are Equality and Markets, Globe and Nation, Liberty and Authority, and Progress and Tradition. The two displayed percentages on each axis add to 100%.
Can a single answer affect more than one axis?
Yes. The answer multiplier, from −1 to +1, is applied to each of the statement’s axis weights. Negative weights reverse the direction of the contribution.
Does 50% identify a political centrist?
A midpoint can come from neutral or unsure answers, or from contributions that cancel. The score cannot determine a political identity, population percentile, or voting choice.
Is the test free? Can I skip questions?
The test, results, and all eight public guides are free without an account. You need all 70 answers for personal scores. You can read the public guides without answering anything.
What gets included when I share?
Copying shares the public test link. It carries no answers, percentages, or ID for your attempt. There is no personal PNG export.
en.formula: Each choice has a multiplier of −1, −0.5, 0, +0.5, or +1. Multiply it by each signed item weight and add contributions to get the sum S for each axis. The absolute weight totals M are 195, 225, 320, and 292. The positive calculation end is 100 × (M + S) ÷ (2 × M), rounded to one decimal. Subtract the displayed value from 100 for the other end.
en.boundary: The adaptation preserves the 70 English statements, five response choices, and scoring weights in the pinned source. FermatMind provides the Chinese translations. This edition has no independently established translation equivalence, reliability, or population norms. It gives no party match, stable ideology classification, or voting recommendation.
